title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reading.body:
This is an impersonation carried out with a synthetic likeness. A caller used an AI deepfake to appear as a sitting chief minister on a WhatsApp video call, and a second person posed as that figure's manager. The fraud then escalated through a third false identity, a person claiming to be a CBI officer. The falsehood was not a model asserting something wrong by accident, it was a fabricated identity presented as real to a specific person.

The failure sits at the point of first contact, on a general-purpose messaging app where a video call carries no proof of who is on the other end. The victim had no independent channel to confirm that the person on screen was the official depicted, and the demands for processing fees, exchange charges and a fine were all made inside that unverified conversation. Catching it would have required confirming the caller's identity through a source outside the call itself, because the deepfake was the only evidence offered that the offer was real.

What is not established is who made the call, whether the deepfake was produced by the same people who collected the money, and whether anyone will be charged. A case was registered under the Information Technology Act, which is a step in a process and not a finding. The account rests on a single outlet's reporting.

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A Bengaluru security guard, Ratikanta Giri, 29, from Odisha, received a WhatsApp video call on Sept 9. The caller used an AI deepfake to appear as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay and offered Rs 11 lakh in financial aid. A person posing as Vijay's manager said Rs 5 lakh was allotted and asked for processing payments. Giri was asked for Rs 5,000 as exchange charges, then paid Rs 18,000 after being told his PIN was locked.

A fake CBI officer then demanded more than Rs 50,000 as a fine. Fearing loss of earlier payments, Giri transferred that and other amounts, losing over Rs 1.04 lakh. When the fraudsters asked for another Rs 50,000, he refused and realized he had been duped. He contacted cybercrime helpline 1930 and Byappanahalli police. A case was registered under the Information Technology Act. Police warned people not to trust such calls or make payments based on them.
